saints.name: St. Cedd
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Northumbrian monk trained at Lindisfarne who evangelized the East Saxons and founded Lastingham…
biography: Cedd was one of four brothers, among them St. Chad, raised and trained in the monastic life at Lindisfarne under St. Aidan. Sent first to the Middle Angles and then to the kingdom of the East Saxons, he preached with such success that he was consecrated their bishop, founding churches and monasteries along the way.

He took part in the Synod of Whitby in 664 and, though schooled in the Celtic tradition, accepted its decision for the Roman observance. Later that year, at the monastery he had established at Lastingham in Yorkshire, he died of the plague. The Venerable Bede preserved his memory.
saints.knownFor: Evangelizing the East Saxons and founding Lastingham.

sources.text: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English People (public domain)
